title: I Used the Band Practice Noise Curfew on the Drummer's Dad

parts.text: I knocked at 10:02 p.m. because the snare was still arguing with my windows. I am forty-four, small-business tired, house next to a garage band. The drummer, Jules, is sixteen and actually good. His dad, Rick, had posted a polite curfew in the neighborhood app: 10 p.m. weeknights, his own idea after a complaint. Tonight Rick was on the kit. Jules was in the driveway on his phone. The garage smelled like rain on hot cymbals. Rick said, "It's just one more song" I said, "Your post said 10" My mug of tea went cold on the fence post. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Rick is still on the kit after his own 10 p.m. post, and Jules is watching from the driveway.

parts.text: Jules mouthed sorry. I held up the app post. Rick laughed, then stopped when two other neighbors appeared in slippers. He packed the snare. The next day he tried to edit the post to 11. The app showed the edit. People quoted 10 anyway. Jules now practices drums at 7, which is better musically too. Rick barbeques quieter. I bring extra tea sometimes, which is how truces look on our block. The cymbals still smell like rain when it hits. I can live with 7 p.m. talent. Neighbor said, "It says 10" Rick said, "Don't be cops" Jules waved. I waved. The fence post still has a tea ring. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened.
